描述_EN: camels and horses were used as pack animals and merchants passed their goods from oasis to oasis. they were recovered from an area now referred to as the silk road, a series of overland trade routes that crossed asia, from china to europe. the victoria and albert museum has around 700 ancient and medieval textiles recovered by stein at the beginning of the twentieth century. these fragments were brought back from central asia by the explorer and archaeologist sir marc aurel stein (1862–1943). the most notable item traded was silk. the silk road was also important for the exchange of ideas – while silk textiles travelled west from china, buddhism entered china from india in this way. they once formed part of a burial face cover and were recovered from the site of astana, an ancient burial ground where the tombs date from the 3rd to the 8th century ad. some are silk while others are made from the wool of a variety of different animals. these three fragments are of monochrome pattern woven buff silk, with one piece sewn to form a frill. the textiles range in date from the second century bc to the twelfth century ad.
描述_ZN: 年，骆驼和马被用作驮运动物，商人们在绿洲之间传递他们的货物。 年，它们被发现于现在被称为丝绸之路的地区，这是一系列横跨亚洲、从中国到欧洲的陆上贸易路线。 年，维多利亚和阿尔伯特博物馆有大约700件古代和中世纪的纺织品，是斯坦在20世纪初找到的。 年，这些碎片被探险家和考古学家Marc Aurel Stein先生（1862-1943）从中亚带回来。 年，最引人注目的贸易项目是丝绸。 年：丝绸之路对思想交流也很重要--当丝绸纺织品从中国向西运输时，佛教也通过这种方式从印度进入中国。 它们曾经构成了一个墓葬面罩的一部分，并在阿斯塔纳遗址中被发现，这是一个古老的墓地，其墓葬年代为公元3-8世纪。 有些是丝绸，有些则是由各种不同动物的羊毛制成。 这三块碎片是单色图案编织的水蓝色丝绸，其中一块缝制成了一个褶皱。 这些纺织品的年代从公元前二世纪到公元十二世纪不等。
